fields.v: Jain, V. (2026). Beyond Benchmarks: Can Small Open-Weight Models Get Real Coding Work Done? An Engineering Journey Through Model Serving, Tool Calling, Runtime Fragmentation, and Verified Coding Tasks. arXiv:2610.34241v1 [cs.SE], 25 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.34241v1 (25 Oct 2026); no published venue stated (record only in the arXiv export)
Independent Researcher, India (single author). Competing interest declared: the author develops self-hosted AI infrastructure with potential commercial applications related to the system examined

Evaluates; secondary: Compares — retrospective empirical systems experience report (July-October 2026) on serving open-weight models for coding agents, with three delegation studies comparing direct frontier coding (Claude Code + Claude Opus 5.5) with delegation to local open-weight workers, scored by hidden behavioural checks

No SDD approach. Configurations: (A) direct frontier coding: Claude Code + Claude Opus 5.5; (B) frontier-to-open-weight delegation: Claude Code + Opus 5.5 parent delegating bounded implementation to a local worker under the author's delegation contract: 'optimized' and 'batch-labeled adaptive' delegation with Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B IQ3 (llama.cpp); Nemotron Cascade 2 and Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B as 4-bit MLX checkpoints. Claude Code version Not stated (changed during the Nemotron study). Clients tried during integration: Cline, OpenCode, Kilo, Continue, Claude Code via the author's gateway

No specification document. Fixed artifact contract for worker output: one JSON object; static checks on imports, exports and exported function parameter lists; parent inspection before application. Worker input: task text, supplied file context (24,000-character gate), artifact contract; parent constraints field not forwarded in the first study

Parent reads repository -> delegates bounded implementation (single or sequential batch packages) -> worker returns artifact -> static validation -> parent inspection -> application -> sealed hidden behavioural checks
None in the studies (review by the frontier parent model; sessions author-operated)
N/A (no SDD approach; delegation workflow run end to end)
Not classifiable (delegation contract, no specification approach); author does not use SDD terms

Existing code base (small synthetic TypeScript fixtures): study 1, five task categories (quote, prorate, customer, split, parts) implemented against supplied file context and stubs; second suite, 15 synthetic TypeScript repositories (3 each of bug fixes, features, multi-file integrations, export-preserving refactors, test-driven repairs) whose stubs fail the sealed check. Integration tests and one observed session partly on a private existing code base
fields.why: The second suite uses small synthetic TypeScript repositories with stubs for bug fixes, refactors, integrations and test-driven repairs (p. 15: 'not a trial on production repositories'); study 1 implements functions against supplied file context. The paper does not frame tasks as new project or existing code base; existing code base kept as best value.
fields.doubt: As tarefas usam repositórios TypeScript sintéticos pequenos com stubs (bug fixes, refactors, features; p. 15). Decide se conta como existing code base ou new project.

Not stated (task names suggest business logic: quotes, prorating, payments, fees, invoices)

Time: TTFT (observational), wall time in one fee pilot (126.4 s delegated vs 27.4 s direct)

Verified trials (task-specific hidden behavioural checks pass); verified worker substitutions (artifact proposed, inspected, applied, sealed check passes, no parent rewrite); 95% Wilson intervals; Student-t interval over task means

Gateway/tool events (parsed tool calls, stop without tool call, empty_content, stream_failed, repetition_cut, job_failed, fallback); median TTFT cold vs warm prefix cache; artifact outcomes (signature rejection, invalid JSON, parent rejection, deadline); post-hoc signature-sensitivity diagnostic

Automatic: sealed hidden behavioural checks; gateway and debug logs; client token usage priced by token class (matched the client's list-price estimate in all 45 trials); second-suite inputs hash-recorded before scoring. Retrospective: author re-checked counts against saved records without re-running; engineering observations from notes

Criterion (per trial): hidden behavioural checks pass (plus artifact acceptance for a substitution); no configuration-level criterion. Values:
- Study 1, direct: Claude Code + Opus 5.5 (baseline): 15/15 verified [0.80, 1.00]; $0.136 per verified success
- Study 1, optimized delegation: Claude Code + Opus 5.5 + Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B IQ3 (llama.cpp): 12/15 [0.55, 0.93]; $0.214
- Study 1, batch-labeled adaptive delegation, same models (only 5/15 used batch calls): 14/15 [0.70, 0.99]; $0.199
- Second suite, direct: Claude Code + Opus 5.5 (baseline): 45/45 (37/45 if 16 replaced spend-limit sessions count as failures); $6.888 total, $0.153 per session and per success
- Second suite, delegation to Nemotron Cascade 2 (MLX 4-bit): 12/45 verified, 11 substitutions (8/45 keep-all); task-mean 0.267 (0.033-0.500); $15.761 total, $0.350 per session, $1.313 per verified success, $1.433 per substitution
- Second suite, Qwen follow-up, delegation to Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B (MLX 4-bit), no direct arm: 0/45; $16.023 total, $0.356 per session; per success undefined
Verdicts: quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors (all configurations)

Tasks: study 1, 5 TypeScript categories; second suite, 15 synthetic TypeScript repositories with sealed checks (stubs fail, references pass). Configurations: direct vs delegation arms above. Baseline: direct frontier coding (none in the Qwen follow-up). Held constant: parent Claude Code + Opus 5.5; task instructions and visible checks; worker contract in second suite (one attempt, 120 s deadline, 4,096 output tokens, temperature 0, 32,768 context, 24,000-character file gate); frozen schedule. Not held constant: Claude Code version changed during Nemotron study; parent prompt cache not reset; Qwen cohort ran later. Repetitions: 3 per task/condition. Human intervention: none during sessions; 16 spend-limit sessions replaced, contrary to the written protocol

Direct coding best on verification and frontier cost in both studies with a direct arm: study 1 15/15 vs 12/15 and 14/15, $0.136 vs $0.214 / $0.199 per verified success; second suite 45/45 vs 12/45 (Nemotron) and 0/45 (Qwen); Nemotron delegation about 8.6x the direct frontier cost per verified success. Study 1 Wilson intervals overlap; no significance tests; author states the data do not establish general success-rate differences

Distinguished direct from delegation clearly in the second suite, not reliably in study 1 (overlapping intervals). Repeatability: 3 repetitions per cell, clustered within tasks. Limitations stated: replacement of 16 sessions, AI-assisted tasks and hidden tests without pre-run snapshot (study 1), not pre-registered, single worker configurations, fixed parent harness, cohorts not contemporaneous, worker constraints not forwarded and prompts truncated in study 1, local cost unmeasured

Limitations: retrospective, nonrandomized evidence; private records; limited task diversity (five TypeScript tasks plus one synthetic suite); no front-end or product-quality metric; limited worker diversity; fixed parent harness; procedural deviation; AI-assisted task and scorer development; incomplete hardware/runtime metadata; cost limited to frontier list price. Gaps: bounded repair attempt after contract rejection (proposed, not run); other harnesses as parents; causal effect of cache changes

Headline results (45/45 direct, 12/45 Nemotron) are the replacement cohort; keep-all counts 37/45 and 8/45 (Section 9.3). Post-hoc: 19 of 36 underscore-only rejected artifacts pass hidden checks unchanged, not counted. Data: records private, not released or offered on request; a sanitized subset may follow review. Not pre-registered (stated). Programming language: TypeScript. Competing interest declared; the delegation workflow and gateway are the author's own. Computing partly on Google Cloud free-trial credits
